facts: Environmental subsystems are central components of operating systems of the Windows NT type.
Environmental subsystems allow the operating system to run software developed for the platform in question.
Windows NT 4.0 has four environmental subsystems.
The environmental subsystems in Windows NT 4.0 include Win32, DOS or Win16, OS/2, and POSIX.
The environmental subsystems are one part of the strategy Microsoft developed for making the Windows NT stream of operating systems a hub for multi-platform computing.
The strategy Microsoft developed for making the Windows NT stream of operating systems a hub for multi-platform computing includes four Hardware Abstraction layers.
The strategy Microsoft developed for making the Windows NT stream of operating systems a hub for multi-platform computing includes a driver for the HPFS, the standard for OS/2.
Since Windows 2000, the FAT32 file system first introduced with Windows 95 has also been present.
HPFS was deprecated and then omitted in later systems.
A third-party driver for FAT32 can be used on the earlier NT operating systems.
Windows NT as of version 4.0 had a default of four file systems, NTFS, HPFS, FAT12, and FAT16.
Installations of Windows NT with a driver allowing access to FAT32 are very common.
Tools allowing access to Unix file systems are also in existence.

Interoperability with Novell Netware is generally implemented at the applications and systems programming level rather than at the kernel and data link layer and therefore further from the physical hardware.
